chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid al-Attar from some of our companions who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman who is doubted [regarding pregnancy], in whom like her gets pregnant and like her does not get pregnant and does not menstruate, and her husband has had intercourse with her; how should he divorce her? He said: 'He should keep her for three months, then divorce her.'
And the divorce of one to whom the man cannot gain access is like the divorce of the absent husband.

key_terms.مَنْ لاَ يَصِلُ اَلرَّجُلُ إِلَيْهَا: One to whom the man cannot gain access

ai.seo_question: How does a husband divorce a woman who does not menstruate and has uncertain pregnancy status?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the *istibra'* (waiting period) for a *mustarah* (woman of uncertain pregnancy status) who does not menstruate, prescribing a three-month retention period before divorce to ensure clarity of lineage. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on removing doubt (*shakk*) in family law, distinguishing this specific case from standard waiting periods by linking the status of an inaccessible woman to that of an absent husband, thereby ensuring procedural fairness in divorce execution.
